scenarios.name: count-accounts
scenarios.why: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ACCOUNT WHERE ACCOUNT_SORTCODE = '987654' (the program's own sort code): SQLCODE 0 -- 'Y' and NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS 13 (the seed's 987654 rows; the 123456 one is not counted)

scenarios.name: caller-data-initialised
scenarios.why: a COMMAREA full of the caller's values: INITIALIZE DFHCOMMAREA blanks / zeroes the named items (not the FILLERs), then the count and 'Y'

scenarios.name: select-fails
scenarios.why: the SELECT fails -913: 'N', NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS left at the INITIALIZE's zero (FAIL-CODE not set)

scenarios.name: select-fails-caller-data
scenarios.why: the SELECT fails -913 over a COMMAREA full of the caller's values (an 8-digit account number among them): INITIALIZE DFHCOMMAREA zeroes the number, NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS and LAST-ACCOUNT-NUMBER, blanks the eye-catcher and fail code, and the failure branch sets only 'N' -- nothing of the caller's survives

scenarios.name: no-commarea
scenarios.why: the caller passes no COMMAREA (EIBCALEN 0, no DFHCOMMAREA): the program still INITIALIZEs and fills DFHCOMMAREA, never testing EIBCALEN

scenarios.name: eibcalen-zero
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN 0 with the COMMAREA record present (X23): the INITIALIZE reaches past the bytes the caller passed

scenarios.name: eibcalen-short
scenarios.why: the caller passed 20 of the 98 bytes: INITIALIZE writes the number at byte 20, past EIBCALEN

scenarios.name: eibcalen-45
scenarios.why: the caller passed 45 bytes: the last item the program writes, ACCOUNT-CONTROL-FAIL-CODE, is byte 46, one past EIBCALEN (X23)

scenarios.name: eibcalen-46
scenarios.why: the caller passed exactly the 46 bytes the program addresses (the eye-catcher through FAIL-CODE): the COMMAREA is stated exact, so the area is cut there and every write fits; the 52 bytes past stay the caller's

scenarios.name: eibcalen-full
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN equals the record (98 bytes, X23): the COMMAREA is stated exact and the INITIALIZE and the count fit

notes: CBSA's account-control service (ACCTCTRL; no program in the corpus LINKs it -- the transaction OCAC is the create-account one, which the program never reads -- so the COMMAREA is its own DFHCOMMAREA, the ACCTCTRL copybook's ACCOUNT-CONTROL-RECORD). It INITIALIZEs the COMMAREA and counts the ACCOUNT rows of the program's own sort code (987654) with SELECT COUNT(*) INTO from Db2 (unqualified: the bind's QUALIFIER, IBMUSER); SQLCODE 0 gives 'Y' and the count in NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS, any other 'N'. POPULATE-TIME-DATE is never PERFORMed (dead code). The table is compared after every scenario. Data: seed.sql is cbsa-creacc's (SYNTHETIC; CONTROL rows left out: only ACCOUNT is created).
